A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ECHO's sparse egocentric human-object interaction framework. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and included appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on BEHAVE, OMOMO and AMASS, including baseline comparisons, sparse-conditioning experiments and ablations in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction experiments, revised comparisons and ablations, hand-tracking dropout tests, and qualitative generalization on Aria Digital Twin.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 replace window-based canonicalization with per-frame head-centric representations and conveyor inference with smooth overlapping-window inpainting. Human root transformation is inferred through head alignment rather than diffused. Binary contacts become continuous, conditioning changes, and training uses clean/noisy modality combinations with synchronized noise. Appendix losses replace object vertex reconstruction with object-motion smoothness.

E1.justification: BEHAVE, OMOMO and AMASS remain the principal training and evaluation datasets. v2 adds intermittent hand-tracking scenarios and qualitative evaluation on one Aria Digital Twin sequence with novel motion and objects (Figure 6), providing a limited extension of the existing HOI task coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 substantially revise the comparator set. Standalone BoDiffusion disappears from both comparisons, and the original AMASS EgoAllo comparison is replaced by EgoAllo+H+O, which also enters the HOI comparison. BoDiffusion+Obj is retained as BoDiffusion+O; that renaming alone is not an addition.

E3.justification: Reported model size, training steps and learning rate change from 47.3M, 400k and 1e-4 to 57.7M, 300k and 5e-4. Contact accuracy replaces quaternion difference in Table 1. Sparse-observation percentages change from 1/5/10/25/100 to 10/25/50/100, and new hand-dropout protocols are introduced. Dataset splits, 30-fps processing and 60-frame training windows remain.

E4.justification: v2 adds hand-dropout robustness tests on both HOI datasets, a smooth-inpainting ablation, and NoAMASS evaluation on AMASS. It removes the NoAuxLoss and NoCan ablations from both dataset-specific ablation tables. Appendix Table S2 also extends the additional-modality analysis to OMOMO.

E5.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported aggregation for Tables 1–2 from four runs to three. Table 1 newly supplies uncertainty values for foot-contact scores. Both versions otherwise retain the same general mean-and-variance reporting approach.

E6.justification: Results are extensively replaced under revised models and settings. ECHO's BEHAVE MPJPE changes from 61.4 mm to 6.8 cm, object vertex error from 29.5 to 33.5 cm, and AMASS MPJPE from 93.9 mm to 7.4 cm. v2 adds contact-accuracy, dropout and additional conditioning results. Changed configurations and comparator membership prevent interpreting these as controlled same-setting gains or losses.

T1.justification: v2 revises mathematical definitions of human state, contacts and egocentric conditioning, changes the loss formulation, and adds explicit guidance and smooth-inpainting equations in Appendix Section 9. These substantially change the formal specification. The new skating equation, Eq. 18, sums consecutive joint positions, which appears inconsistent with its stated skating-penalty purpose.

C1.justification: The first unified sparse-tracking HOI framework claim remains. However, the abstract, introduction and conclusion replace the conveyor-inference contribution with smooth inpainting, remove the standalone novelty claim for the head-centric representation, and explicitly add robustness claims concerning intermittent hand tracking and sensor noise.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of overlap blending and training stability, interprets substantial hand-tracking degradation as emerging around 75% missing input, and refines limitations concerning dynamic environments, finger detail and missing RGB-based datasets. The central interpretations about contacts connecting modalities and AMASS supplying human-motion priors remain.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands implementation documentation: rotary embeddings, AMASS conditioning tokens, guidance weights and update scale, a 30-frame overlap, and blending factor 0.4 are specified. Loss weights, training hardware and timing reports are revised; inference timing now includes guidance. Both versions still promise future code and model release.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly positions its representation as extending EgoAllo and its inference as extending HMD2, replacing the earlier conveyor lineage through Diffusion Forcing and The Matrix. Related work adds distinctions from EgoGrasp and WHOLE and expands coverage of recent egocentric methods. These change methodological attribution and positioning beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method exposition and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Related work gains numbered subsections, and the appendix gains a roadmap and separate implementation-details and metrics sections. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond edits required by the new experiments.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. Figures 2–4 are substantially redrawn; qualitative comparisons are reorganized between Figure 5 and Figure S1 with an added comparator. Figure 6 and dropout tables are added, while existing tables receive revised columns, rows and captions.

improvement.justification: The dropout experiments, HOI-adapted EgoAllo comparison and fuller inference documentation provide a modest net improvement in empirical support and reproducibility. Benefits are tempered by removal of motion-only comparisons and two ablations, the apparent skating-equation error, and Table S2's blanket contact-conditioning claim despite better OMOMO object errors with human conditioning. These limitations prevent a clear substantial overall improvement.
